key_insight: Augment primitive-based 3D representations (e.g., Gaussian splats) with neural harmonic textures that attach high-frequency latent features to a virtual scaffold, enabling faithful reconstruction of fine detail while preserving the scalability and flexibility of primitives.
problem_solved: Primitive-based reconstructions struggle to represent high-frequency surface detail because individual primitives have limited expressivity; this work addresses how to encode and render fine textures from a primitive-centric representation.
method: Anchor learnable latent feature vectors to a virtual scaffold tied to the primitive representation, providing localized, continuous feature support.
Use a harmonic (frequency-aware) neural texture encoding to represent high-frequency appearance information compactly and robustly.

Integrate the neural harmonic textures with primitive-based rendering (e.g., 3D Gaussian splatting) and jointly optimize geometry, feature anchors, and appearance for high-quality novel-view synthesis.
impact: Enables practitioners to get the scalability and efficiency of primitive-based neural reconstructions while recovering much finer visual detail, improving novel-view quality for large scenes and downstream tasks like relighting or editing.

paper_title: Neural Harmonic Textures for High-Quality Primitive Based Neural Reconstruction
paper_authors: Jorge Condor, Nicolas Moenne-Loccoz, Merlin Nimier-David, Piotr Didyk, Zan Gojcic
